overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: minutes were approved timely and are sufficiently detailed, no meeting was shown to have occurred, and a new minutes-response allegation was declined. Time and place omissions were noted and amendment encouraged.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve minutes of six meetings from July to December 2022.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board approved all five sets of minutes in a timely manner and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law as all five sets of minutes were approved within the later of the next three Board meetings or 30 days following each Board meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged five sets of minutes lacked a list of documents used at each meeting, making them insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we are constrained to find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law and that the minutes are sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complaint: the AG noted the minutes omit the meeting time and place and encouraged amendment.
allegations.key_passage: Meeting minutes must include the location of the meeting, as well as the actual scheduled time of each meeting and not just the time that the chair opened the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to post notice for, and create minutes of, meetings held at a fire dump site and at a court location.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find insufficient evidence to conclude that a meeting, as defined by the Open Meeting Law, occurred.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant said the Board failed to respond to a request for meeting minutes, which was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this allegation was not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review its merits.
